title: Data Infra hire sprint + blind-skill rubric
content:
Goal: run a 4-week hiring sprint to hire 2 mid-senior Data Infrastructure Engineers (IC3-IC4). Focus: fast, fair, skills-first assessment with blind scoring on take-home and pair exercise. Integrate onboarding checklist to shorten time-to-first-deploy to 45 days.

Summary timeline:
- Week 0: role posting, sourcing brief + scorecard published to hiring team.
- Week 1: screen blitz (30m HM screens) + send take-home to top candidates.
- Week 2: take-home blind scoring + first technical loop (system design 60m).
- Week 3: pair-programming (remote, 90m) + behavioral/culture loop (30m).
- Week 4: final calibration + offers to top 2. Buffer for backups: extend to week 5 if needed.

Sourcing brief (for recruiters):
- Role: Data Infrastructure Engineer (focus: streaming infra, high-throughput ETL, ops).
- Must-have: production experience with Kafka/streaming, Kubernetes, observability stacks (Prometheus/Grafana/Tempo or equivalent).
- Nice-to-have: Rust/Go for infra tooling, experience with model-serving pipelines or large-scale KV caches.
- Compensation band: IC3: 170-200k base, IC4: 200-240k base (US market) + equity and benefits.
- Diversity/outreach note: prioritize sourcing from underrepresented talent pools; blind take-home reduces bias.

Interview loop & roles:
- Recruiter screen (30m): logistics, comp, work authorization, basic fit. Owner: Talent Partner.
- Hiring manager screen (30m): high-level system experience, scope, leadership signals. Owner: Eng Manager.
- Take-home exercise (48-72h, optional 72h extension): small infra problem; candidates submit code + short writeup. Anonymized before scoring. Owner: People Ops to anonymize, Applied ML lead to curate exercise.
- System design (60m): whiteboard/diagram; evaluate tradeoffs for high-throughput ingestion + schema evolution. Interviewers: Senior Data Infra + Platform Eng.
- Pair-programming (90m): remote pair on a focused infra task (tests + small refactor). Record for quality control but not for candidate review. Interviewers: peer IC.
- Culture/behavior (30m): ownership, communication, incident response stories. Interviewers: cross-functional PM or SRE.
- Final bar-raiser (30m): senior architect to validate technical bar.

Blind scoring rules (take-home):
- Submission pipeline: candidates upload to GH gist or zip; recruiter strips name/email and assigns random ID; files placed on private drive for blind reviewers.
- Reviewers: 3 reviewers (1 senior infra, 1 peer, 1 product/pm for impact). Each reviewer scores independently.
- Scoring matrix (0-4 scale per category): correctness (40%), code quality & tests (20%), system thinking & tradeoffs (25%), documentation & clarity (15%). Weighting applied to normalized average.
- Minimum pass to progress: weighted score >= 2.6/4 and no category below 1.5. Tie-breaker: system design and pair-programming performance.

Live interview rubric (system design / pair):
- Categories and guidance (0-4 scale):
  - Problem framing & requirements clarity (20%): did candidate clarify latency/cost/SLAs? Ask for constraints.
  - Architecture & component selection (25%): appropriateness of Kafka vs pub/sub, durable stores, buffers.
  - Operational considerations (20%): monitoring, alerting, runbook, scaling strategy.
  - Correctness & edge cases (15%): idempotency, late arriving data, schema changes.
  - Communication & tradeoffs (20%): clear tradeoff discussion, estimations.
- Passing threshold: weighted score >= 3.0/4 with no category below 2.0 for IC4; >=2.6 for IC3.

Interviewer logistics + calibration:
- All interviewers get rubric PDF + 5 sample scored take-homes this sprint for calibration.
- Use shared scoring sheet (link in linked_artifacts) and leave 3 short comments: "strengths", "risks", "recommended outcome".
- Post-interview debrief: 24h window to submit scores; panel meets within 72h for calibration.

Offer decision policy:
- Hire 2 if both meet bar. If 1 meets bar, consider second from backlog with explicit approval from Eng Director.
- Compensation approvals needed: Hiring manager + People Ops lead signoff.
- Counter-offer window: aim to close within 7 business days.

Onboarding checklist (0-60 days): high-level, actionable, owner tags included.
- Day 0: welcome email, pre-onboard access requests submitted (IT), Slack + calendar invites. Owner: People Ops.
- Day 1: laptop + corp accounts, corp orientation, basics: repo access, infra Slack channels (#data-infra, #oncall). Owner: IT + People Ops.
- Week 1 goals: dev environment up, run local ingestion pipeline end-to-end, read runbooks. Owner: Mentor.
- Week 2 goals: own a small bugfix or monitoring alert triage, introduce in team demo. Owner: Mentor + EM.
- Week 3–4: take on a small scoped ticket to improve production telemetry (observable improvement in SLI or reduced noise). Owner: Mentor + SRE buddy.
- Week 5–8: lead a rollout of a non-critical config change through staging, validation, and rollout. Owner: Hiring manager.
- By Day 45–60: expected to independently own at least one on-call rotation ticket and a small feature.

Mentor rotation schedule (reduce single-point mentor risk):
- Primary mentor: first 4 weeks (technical ramp + first deliverable).
- Secondary mentor: weeks 3–8 (focus on culture, product context, cross-team contacts).
- 2-week pairing blocks with SRE and Data Platform in weeks 2 and 5.

Documents & quick links new hires must read (ordered):
1) Oncall runbook (CONFLUENCE:INFRA-ONCALL-RUNBOOK)
2) Data infra architecture overview (CONFLUENCE:DATA-ARCH-2024)
3) Deployment playbook + CI template (GH:repo/deploy-playbook)
4) Security checklist for infra changes (SEC-OPS:SC-7)

Notes to interviewers / light-weight SOPs:
- Keep feedback behaviorally anchored: cite examples from the interview.
- Avoid early disqualification for school/company names; focus on demonstrated skills.
- For take-home, do not penalize style differences (e.g., language choice) if correctness and tradeoffs clear.

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we allow take-home in a containerized (Docker) deliverable or prefer source + tests? Current preference: source + tests; Docker allowed but reviewers should not require running containers.
- Should we run a paid take-home for candidates unable to commit time? Consider stipend for full-day exercises.
- Calibration: run a 45-minute interviewer calibration session week before sprint. Confirmed? (Action: Sofia to schedule)

Candidate experience checklist (to reduce drop-off):
- Clear timeline in first email (what to expect + timeline).
- Max 72h for take-home to reduce fatigue.
- Provide feedback within 10 business days for non-offer rejections.

Post-hire retro items to capture at EOY:
- Drop-off rates by stage, median time-to-offer, offer acceptance reasons, quality of hire signals at 60d (mentor + manager survey).

Appendix: sample take-home prompt (short sketch)
- "Design and implement a small ingestion service that reads events from a mock 'user-events' stream, deduplicates by event_id, writes to a simple durable store, and exposes a metric endpoint for processed events per minute. Include tests and a short README describing deployment and failure modes."

- Example reviewer checklist for take-home: runs tests locally (yes/no), all edge cases covered (list), readme clarity (0-4), performance consideration (0-4), suggested improvements.

Draft action items (owners):
- Sofia: finalize take-home prompt + schedule calibration session by 2025-02-14.
- Liam: create job posting + diversity outreach list by 2025-02-12.
- Priya: set up anonymization pipeline for submissions by 2025-02-17.

Last notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and lightweight—iterate after first sprint. Keep the rubric public to interviewers but not to candidates (to preserve assessment fidelity).

Unresolved: stipend policy, Docker requirement, final calibration date.
